correctness.rationale: The point localization follows by enumerating endpoint types: point–point intervals have no intermediate points; point–line and line–line intermediate points lie on a selected endpoint line. Thus q²≤a+qb. At size q, equality forces q disjoint lines, a parallel class; length-four intervals between two such lines cover their points and each transversal. At size q+1 for q≥3, at least q lines are selected. An incomplete class containing s≥2 selected lines leaves a missing class line with at most q+1−s covered points. With q pairwise intersecting lines, their union plus one point covers at most q²−q+2<q²; with q+1 pairwise intersecting lines, no unselected line is on a shortest path. This proves the extension classification and count without double counting. At q=2 identify line vertices with subdivided edges of K4 on the four points. Intersecting selected lines AB and AC force the selected point to be D, and the resulting intervals miss line BC. A selected line AB with points C,D covers CD by their connecting geodesic and all four cross lines by the point–line geodesics. These give exactly six minimal triples in addition to 24 extensions. Distinct classes are disjoint as vertex sets, so the exchange threshold and graphs follow directly.
residual_risks: The finite checks concern coordinate examples; the proof only assumes the stated axioms of an existing plane. The exclusion of minimal sets is only at cardinality q+1.
